panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Implied 14-17% looks roughly fair-to-slightly-cheap. Historical post-emergence realised mean abs is 15.2% (-18.2%, -9.7%, +17.6%) and this is the first fiscal-year-end print plus the first FY27 framing from Feurle/van Issum, so I model realised ~15-20% with a fat left tail. The move size is priced; the direction is not.
key_drivers: The bar is guidance, not consensus, and consensus is broken: company guided Q4 FY26 revenue $140-160M with gross margin still negative and opex flat ~$61M, yet screen consensus is fragmented -- TradingView carries -$2.45 EPS on $150.0M revenue while an Investing.com preview cites -$0.52 on $223.6M, a figure incompatible with the company's own guide.

Underlying KPIs are deteriorating, not inflecting: Q3 FY26 revenue $150.2M (-10.6% q/q, -19% y/y, third straight decline). Non-GAAP GM -21% / GAAP -27%, adj EBITDA -$62M, underutilization drag ~$46M, FCF ~-$90M on $1.165B cash.

The metric this trades on is the Q1 FY27 revenue guide plus the non-GAAP gross-margin path, not Q4 EPS. A flat/down Q1 guide with GM still near -20% is a down print; a beat is already required just to stay flat.

Offsetting the fundamentals: 24.4-24.5M shares short = ~47% of shares out and ~80.7% of float, with a ~933% annualised borrow fee and ~100% utilisation. Anything not-worse-than-feared mechanically squeezes that base.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The squeeze overwhelms the fundamentals: with ~80% of float short at a ~933% borrow fee and the stock already -59% from its May high, an in-line ~$150M quarter paired with a credible gross-margin roadmap forces covering and lifts the stock 15-20% even though revenue declined again -- exactly the Q3 pattern, where a 28% 'miss' printed +17.6%.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Estimate-revision breadth is snippet_only and conflicting across providers ($150M vs $223.6M revenue base); Q4 design-in dollar totals and any FY2027 guidance framework were unavailable pre-print.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Front-expiry straddle prices roughly +-14% (Bloomberg via Investing.com) to +-17.3% (Benzinga/TradingView) quoted off a ~$31-32 spot -- at or below the post-emergence realised history (mean abs 15.18%, median 17.61%, max 18.22%) and below 30-day HV of 133.65% vs IV of 122.65% (Barchart). IV Rank only 13.39%. Spot has already broken to $27.91 (-11.28% intraday, 2026-08-19 11:57 EDT, stockanalysis.com). I expect a realised move of 18-25%, larger than the 14-17% priced. Own gamma, do not sell it.
key_drivers: Positioning is maximally short into a stock that has already dumped ~20% in three sessions: 24.50M shares short = 47.14% of shares outstanding and 80.66% of float, short ratio 5.81 days (stockanalysis.com, 2026-08-19).

Flow is call-tilted while the tape is red: Barchart put/call volume ratio 0.42 (2,843 puts vs 6,697 calls) against near-balanced OI ratio 0.94. Dealers short those upside calls are short gamma above spot, amplifying an up-gap.

Borrow data is in open conflict: Fintel/OptionsTradingReport show 932.81% fee with ~1K shares available (2026-08-15), while ChartExchange's live IBKR feed shows 1.93% with 200,000 shares available (2026-08-19 11:44 EDT). Either reading tilts the tail up.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: A balance-sheet event on the call -- a dilutive equity raise, a going-concern qualification, or an FY2027 guide that kills the AI-data-centre narrative -- gaps this 25%+ regardless of short positioning; shorts do not cover into an announced offering, they add.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Dealer gamma exposure / gamma-flip level and skew direction unsourced (Barchart GEX rendered client-side, no data). Borrow fee contradictory across sources by three orders of magnitude; short-interest settlement dates undisclosed. Implied-move quotes predate today's ~11% drawdown and are anchored to a ~$31-32 spot, not $27.91.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Expect a realised +-15-20% move; the 14-17% implied straddle looks fairly priced to marginally cheap given 138% IV matched by 47% short interest and a genuinely binary AI-narrative print. No edge in owning the straddle; the edge, if any, is fading the retail call crowd rather than betting on magnitude.
key_drivers: Retail attention has decayed, not built: AltIndex shows ~58 Stocktwits mentions/day, down ~91% over three months; Reddit runs ~8 mentions/day (6th percentile among semis). This is a niche squeeze trade, not a live meme -- the May mania that took the stock to $80.82 has already left, and the stock is ~61% off that high.

The narrative is fragile and sentiment-only: the bull story rests on the Aug 6 LITEON 800VDC 'qualification' partnership with no disclosed revenue, against negative ~17.4% gross margin and a distress score of 85/100. Retail is expressing it through 138%-IV calls with ~17% bid-ask spreads -- the most expensive possible way to be right.

Sell-side tone is shifting negative into the event: Susquehanna cut to $30 from $40 (Hold), Morgan Stanley to $23 from $26 (Equal Weight), mean target $30 sits below spot, and shares broke ~5-10% lower on Aug 17-18 with no positive catalyst.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The positioning is among the most squeeze-prone in a liquid semi name -- 47% of shares out short at a 932.81% annualised borrow, meaning a flat stock bleeds shorts. A quantified hyperscaler/800VDC design-win number or a beat with a credible margin path detonates that gradient.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: No clean Stocktwits time series for 7/14/30-day deltas; Aug 17-18 price/session data conflicting (-10.01% vs -5.01% across aggregators); short-interest percentage varies by source and settlement date.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Base rate on the only three usable prints is mean abs 15.2% / median 17.6% (-18.22%, -9.71%, +17.61%), so the 14-17% implied is roughly fair to marginally cheap. Direction is close to a coin flip -- I do not think the implied size is mispriced enough to be the trade.
key_drivers: Post-emergence sample is n=3 only (successor equity began trading 2025-09-29): 1 up / 2 down = 33% up, far too thin to call a tilt; treat as ~45-50/50 with a whisper of down.

Gap-and-drift has been continuation, 3 for 3, and the current regime is negative -- down 61% from the May peak and -10.0% on 2026-08-17 into the print -- the single mechanical reason for a small negative lean.

The fundamentals-to-direction mapping is broken in this name: last quarter WOLF missed EPS by ~6x and revenue by 28% and still closed +17.6%, on 46.98% of shares out short at a 932% borrow. That is why prob_up is not pushed below the mid-40s.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The short-side structure -- a 47%-of-shares-out short base paying a 932% borrow into a 138% IV event is the textbook setup for a violent upside gap on a merely in-line quarter, exactly what happened in May on far worse numbers.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: No clean quarter-by-quarter reaction table for the predecessor Cree/Wolfspeed equity; the 2025-09-29 Chapter 11 emergence is a genuine structural break that voids the pre-2025 base rate; could not verify the 2026-08-17 -10% move's cause, nor obtain a same-day spot refresh.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: +-14-17% implied is roughly fair to marginally cheap. Realised sample is mean abs 15.2% / median 17.6%, ATM IV >138%, and 47% of shares out are short -- expect 15-18% realised with a fat right tail. Macro is a tiebreaker, not the dominant term, since a 14-17% idiosyncratic move dwarfs any plausible sector-beta contribution.
key_drivers: Peer demand read-through is good but the reaction read-through is bad: onsemi beat and rose AH; STMicro beat and still fell; Infineon posted record revenue and gave it back; Navitas beat and fell ~12% with a subsequent Underweight PT cut. In this tape, good SiC news is not being paid for.

Factor regime is squarely against this name: SOX fell 5% on Aug 18 as 30y yields hit multi-decade highs; chipmakers slipped again Aug 19 even as the broad tape rebounded. WOLF's exposure -- micro-float, deeply unprofitable, high-beta, AI-narrative -- is the exact basket being de-rated.

Positioning overwhelms the fundamental print and cuts the other way: on the May print WOLF missed revenue by ~28% and still rose +17.6% on AI-datacenter narrative, capping how much the macro read can be worth.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The squeeze: with ~47% of shares out short at a 932% borrow, a single narrative item -- an AI-datacenter revenue target, a hyperscaler supply agreement, or an FY27 guide implying utilisation recovery -- forces covering into no float, and the May precedent proves the market will buy this stock through a large miss.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: No WOLF-specific index/ETF flow or rebalance event found; short interest and borrow fee are snippet-only from a secondary aggregator; intraday Aug 19 tape is from live blogs written before the close.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Implied 14-17% looks too low. WOLF has exceeded its implied move on both recent post-emergence prints. With an 80%-of-float short base and effectively one covering analyst, I expect realised |move| of 20-25% and would treat the straddle as cheap.
panel_verdicts.consensus_view_as_i_read_it: The obvious view is bearish: the AI-datacenter melt-up to $80.82 has deflated ~65%; revenue has declined y/y three quarters running; Q4 guided flat/down with negative gross margin; Susquehanna cut its target, mean PT $30 sits below spot. Plain read: Q4 confirms no inflection and the de-rating continues.
panel_verdicts.strongest_reversal_case: 24.5M shares short = 80.66% of the 30.37M float, 5.81 days to cover, hard borrow. This exact setup already resolved upward once: on the May print WOLF reported a 28% revenue shortfall and the stock rose sharply anyway on AI-datacenter narrative. With coverage down to ~one analyst, the aggregator bar is not the real bar, and a merely-not-worse quarter plus any credible FY27 AI-revenue framing can force a covering cascade into a float that has just been pressed 20% lower in two sessions.
panel_verdicts.what_would_break_my_reversal_case: An FY27 outlook that keeps gross margin negative through the year on a sub-$600M revenue run-rate, or any new equity/ATM raise announced with the print -- either gives shorts a fresh fundamental catalyst.
key_drivers: Positioning: 80.66% of float short, 5.81 days to cover, hard borrow, into a 20% two-day pre-print drawdown
Real bar is company guidance ($140-160M, negative GM), not the stale ~$223.6M aggregator number; coverage is down to ~1 analyst
Offsetting cap: ~24M shares registered for resale (Renesas stake, converts, pre-funded warrants) -- roughly 80% of float in latent supply
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The first post-restructuring FY2027 guide is the single most dangerous item on the call -- a realistic one (continued negative gross margin, cash burn against -$666M net cash) turns a squeeze setup into a solvency debate, exactly as happened on the -18.22% print.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: No specific catalyst found for the ~20% two-session drop; if idiosyncratic rather than pre-print de-risking, the squeeze case weakens. Borrow fee/availability is snippet-only. No FY2027 guidance figures or updated cash balance obtainable pre-print; aggregator EPS estimates conflict.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: The ~14-17% event-implied move looks too cheap. WOLF exceeded its implied move in both of its last two prints; a +-18-25% outcome is my base case. Spot: the $31.46 anchor is stale -- two independent sources show WOLF at ~$27.9, down ~11% intraday on 2026-08-19. Direction I do not have an edge on; magnitude I do.
key_drivers: Insider track is empty in both directions -- four Form 4s all year, all Code F tax-withholding dispositions or grants, no 10b5-1 activity found. Zero informational edge from Section 16.

Structural short/dilution mechanics dominate direction: ~23.7-24.4M shares short (~47% of shares outstanding), reported borrow ~932% with ~1K shares available, and unusual call volume (+160% vs average). But June resale registrations on the 2031 converts mean much of that short interest is likely convert-arb delta hedging, not directional bears.

Communication forensics lean mildly negative: AI narrative substituting for a soft auto book, three layers of hedging language on the Q3 call, and no FY2027 guidance frame at a fiscal year-end print. The register is now dominated by market makers and arbs rather than conviction longs.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The May 2026 precedent directly refutes a fundamentals-driven bearish read: a ~28% revenue miss and the stock still squeezed higher. With ~47% of shares outstanding short and ~1K shares borrowable, any single constructive datapoint can take this 20%+ higher regardless of the P&L.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: No Rule 10b5-1 plan activity found. shortinteresttracker.com 403'd; borrow-fee figure rests on a single low-tier source and should be treated as directionally right, not precise. No specific news catalyst identified for the ~11% intraday drop on 2026-08-19.

synthesis.move_band_note: unsigned magnitude band, right-skewed; the implied move is roughly one standard deviation, not a cap
synthesis.early_prediction: No directional edge: consensus -6.4, and none of the seven personas independently scored beyond |18| in either direction. The soft lean is negative -- a third straight revenue decline, still-negative gross margin, and a Q4 guide that offers no FY27 frame -- but it is fully offset by an extreme short base (~47% of shares outstanding per one un-settlement-dated aggregator) that squeezed this identical setup upward in May despite a 28% revenue miss. Main driver: no persona has an edge on which force wins. Main caveat: reversal risk is High (68.9 consensus, red-team 72) precisely because the mechanism that would break any directional call -- a covering squeeze or a solvency-driven selloff -- is large and symmetric.
synthesis.red_team_survival_note: The red-team case (a covering squeeze into ~80% of float short, which already happened once on worse fundamentals) is specific and sourced, not generic pessimism, and earns its 1.5x weight -- consensus_reversal_risk (68.9) and the High tier reflect that. It does not overturn the panel's lean: five of seven personas independently reached a negative score by different routes (fundamentals, sentiment/positioning-fade, macro/peer read-through, base rates, forensics/communication) after being shown the same squeeze mechanics. The thesis survives as 'no edge with elevated reversal risk on both sides,' not as a confident call in either direction.
synthesis.chair_independence_note: Six of the seven personas independently found and cited the same secondary short-interest aggregator (optionstradingreport.com: ~47% of shares outstanding short, ~932% annualised borrow fee) as as of 2026-06-04/08-15, and the Options persona separately flagged a live IBKR/ChartExchange borrow feed showing ~1.93% fee with 200,000 shares available as of 2026-08-19 -- a three-orders-of-magnitude conflict neither source resolves. That single figure is therefore load-bearing across most of the panel's reversal-risk reasoning despite not being independently corroborated, even though the personas' directional conclusions from it diverged in both sign and magnitude. Certainty is not further reduced for this beyond what the formula already applies, because the panel's directional spread (12 to -18) shows the shared fact was weighed differently, not copied into a shared opinion.

independence_note: Seven isolated subagents; each received only the Phase-0 anchors (ticker, company, event window/session/date, spot, event-implied move, historical realised moves) and nothing else -- no stage-2 dossier, no preliminary direction score, no other persona's verdict, no chair view. See synthesis.chair_independence_note for a caveat on shared secondary sourcing of the short-interest figure.
